name: Nivolumab (adjuvant, single agent)
cyclesNote: Adjuvant intent: continued for about 1 year (or until recurrence / unacceptable toxicity). A 480 mg every-4-weeks schedule is an accepted alternative to 240 mg every 2 weeks.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Nivolumab is a PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor. Adjuvant use follows radical cystectomy for high-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma (>= pT3 / pN+, or residual >= ypT2 / ypN+ after neoadjuvant cisplatin, or cisplatin-ineligible high-risk disease). No companion biomarker test is required to treat, though PD-L1 status is often reported.

supportiveCare: Monitor for immune-related adverse events across organ systems (skin, colon, liver, endocrine glands, lungs, kidney); manage with holds and corticosteroids per severity.
Baseline and periodic thyroid, adrenal, and glucose assessment for endocrinopathies.
Educate the patient to report new diarrhea, dyspnea, jaundice, or rash promptly.
monitoring: thyroid function (TSH/free T4) at baseline and periodically
liver function before each cycle (immune hepatitis)
clinical assessment for colitis, pneumonitis, dermatitis, and endocrinopathy each visit

doseModificationRules.text: Hold nivolumab and start corticosteroids for grade 2-3 immune-related toxicity; resume after recovery to grade <= 1 and steroid taper. Physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 4 or recurrent grade 3 immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Permanently discontinue for grade 4 or recurrent severe immune-related toxicity per labeling; obtain specialty review.

drugs.name: Nivolumab
drugs.notes: Nivolumab 240 mg IV flat dose on day 1 of a 14-day cycle, continued in the adjuvant setting for about 1 year. An alternative flat schedule gives 480 mg IV every 4 weeks. Standard checkpoint-inhibitor immune-related toxicity monitoring applies. Dose per standard urothelial adjuvant practice (Standard Guidelines / DeVita / Harrison, general reference).

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, adjuvant immunotherapy for high-risk MIBC
